title: Creamy Garlic Pasta
summary: Silky garlic cream, burst cherry tomatoes and fresh basil — a 25-minute weeknight favourite.

steps.text: Boil the fettuccine in well-salted water for 10 minutes until al dente. Keep a mug of pasta water, then drain.
Warm the olive oil over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant — don't let it brown.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until they start to burst.
Pour in the cream and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta and parmesan, loosening with a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Tear over the basil, season with salt and pepper, and serve straight away.

title: Chicken Avocado Quinoa Bowl
summary: Smoky chicken, lemony quinoa, avocado and spinach. High protein and ready in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 250 ml salted water for 12 minutes, then cover and rest.
Rub the chicken with paprika, salt and half the oil. Cook in a hot pan for 5 minutes on each side.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, then slice.
Fluff the quinoa with the lemon juice and remaining oil.
Build bowls with spinach, quinoa, chicken, avocado and tomatoes.

title: Tomato Basil Penne
summary: Fresh tomato sauce with garlic and basil. Mild enough for kids — add chilli at the table.

steps.text: Cook the penne in salted water for 11 minutes, then drain, keeping a little water.
Fry the garlic in the olive oil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 12 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the pasta and basil, adding pasta water if needed.
Serve with parmesan if you like.

title: Lemon Herb Salmon
summary: Oven-baked salmon with garlic, lemon and oregano on crisp broccoli.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the broccoli with half the oil and salt on a tray and roast for 8 minutes.
Mix the garlic, oregano, lemon zest and remaining oil. Spread over the salmon.
Add the salmon to the tray and roast for 12 minutes until it flakes.
Squeeze over lemon juice and serve.

title: Berry Ricotta Pancakes
summary: Fluffy ricotta pancakes with warm berries — a slow weekend breakfast.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and sugar in a bowl.
Beat in the eggs, ricotta and milk until just combined.
Melt a little butter in a pan and cook ladlefuls for 2 minutes on each side.
Warm the berries in the pan for 1 minute and spoon over with maple syrup.

title: Caprese Pasta Salad
summary: Tomatoes, mozzarella and basil with fusilli — lunchbox friendly.

steps.text: Cook the fusilli for 10 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the olive oil, balsamic and a pinch of salt.
Toss the pasta with tomatoes, mozzarella, basil and dressing.

title: Harissa Salmon Skillet
summary: Salmon, chickpeas and courgette in one pan with warming harissa.

steps.text: Soften the onion and courgette in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas, tomatoes and half the harissa. Cook for 4 minutes.
Brush the salmon with the rest of the harissa, nestle into the pan, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Finish with lemon and parsley.

title: Pesto Farfalle with Burst Tomatoes
summary: Basil pesto, blistered tomatoes and toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Cook the farfalle for 11 minutes and drain, keeping a splash of water.
Blister the tomatoes in the olive oil for 4 minutes.
Toss the pasta with pesto, tomatoes and a little pasta water.
Top with parmesan and pine nuts.

title: Harvest Chicken Salad
summary: Crunchy leaves, quinoa, avocado and chicken with a lemon dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the olive oil and lemon juice with a pinch of salt.
Toss the leaves, quinoa, carrot and tomatoes with half the dressing.
Top with chicken and avocado and drizzle over the rest.

title: Rustic Tomato Pappardelle
summary: Wide ribbons of pasta in a slow-cooked tomato and garlic sauce.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the passata and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the pappardelle for 8 minutes and toss through the sauce.
Finish with basil and parmesan.

title: Palak Paneer
summary: Soft paneer in a bright, gently spiced spinach gravy.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, cool in iced water and blend with the chilli into a smooth puree.
Heat the ghee, crackle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 1 minute, then the tomatoes for 4 minutes.
Stir in the spinach puree and garam masala and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fold in the paneer and cream, warm through for 2 minutes and season.

title: Chana Masala
summary: Tangy, warming chickpea curry — freezes beautifully.

steps.text: Crackle the cumin seeds in hot oil for 30 seconds, then cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the spices for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the chickpeas and 250 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas.
Finish with coriander leaves.

title: Masala Oats
summary: Savoury oats with vegetables and gentle spice — ready in 15 minutes.

steps.text: Pop the mustard seeds in hot oil for 30 seconds, then cook the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot, peas, tomato and spices and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oats and water and simmer for 4 minutes until creamy.
Top with coriander.

title: Vegetable Poha
summary: Light flattened-rice breakfast with peas, potato and lemon.

steps.text: Rinse the poha in a sieve and leave to soften for 5 minutes.
Pop the mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil for 30 seconds.
Cook the onion, potato and chilli for 5 minutes, then add the peas and turmeric.
Fold in the poha and warm through for 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon, coriander and peanuts if you eat them.

title: Moong Dal Cheela
summary: Protein-rich lentil pancakes with ginger and onion.

ingredients.text: 1 cup yellow moong dal, soaked for 4 hours

steps.text: Blend the soaked dal with the ginger, chilli and a little water into a smooth batter.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin, onion, coriander and salt.
Spread a ladleful on a hot greased pan and cook for 2 minutes on each side.

title: Paneer Tikka Wrap
summary: Charred yoghurt-marinated paneer and peppers in a warm wrap.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, tikka masala and chilli powder and coat the paneer. Leave for 10 minutes.
Char the paneer, pepper and onion in the hot oil for 6 minutes.
Warm the wraps for 30 seconds each.
Fill with lettuce and the paneer mix and roll up.

title: Egg Fried Rice
summary: Day-old rice, eggs and vegetables tossed hot and fast.

steps.text: Scramble the eggs in half the oil for 1 minute and set aside.
Fry the garlic and vegetables in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and fry for 4 minutes, breaking up clumps.
Return the eggs, add soy sauce and sesame oil, and finish with spring onions.

title: Greek Yoghurt Berry Parfait
summary: Thick yoghurt, honey, berries and crunchy granola in five minutes.

steps.text: Layer the yoghurt, berries and granola in a glass.
Drizzle with honey and eat straight away.

title: Chaat Masala Makhana
summary: Crunchy roasted lotus seeds — a light, tangy snack.

steps.text: Roast the makhana in the ghee over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until crisp.
Toss with chaat masala and salt and cool before storing.

title: Hummus & Crunchy Veg
summary: Silky homemade hummus with carrot and cucumber sticks.

steps.text: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic, oil and 3 tbsp cold water until smooth.
Season and serve with the vegetable sticks.

title: Red Lentil & Carrot Soup
summary: Velvety, cumin-scented soup that costs almost nothing to make.

steps.text: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth and finish with lemon juice.

title: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. Great for brunch.

steps.text: Soften the onion and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 6 minutes until the whites set.
Top with feta and parsley.
